Research Work

Doctoral Research

IIT Jodhpur · With Brahadeesh Sankarnarayanan (IIT Jodhpur) and Saraswati Girish Nanoti (IISc)

Majority Game Coloring of Trees: A majority coloring of a graph is a vertex coloring in which each vertex has at most half of its neighbors sharing its color. Lovász showed in 1966 that two colors always suffice for any finite graph. In the majority coloring game, two players alternately color vertices while maintaining the majority condition. The least number of colors for which the first player has a winning strategy is the majority game chromatic number \( \mu_g(G) \). While this number is unbounded for general graphs, it is at most four for trees. We study \( \mu_g(T) \) using a configuration-based strategy that prevents a small family of local obstruction patterns.

An interactive Tree Coloring Explorer is available for experimenting with majority colorings on trees.

Built with vertices, edges and curiosity.
